title: HIPAA-AI Compliance Specification v1.0
description: Machine-readable specification defining what the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) requires from AI systems that process Protected Health Information (PHI). Each control maps to a HIPAA rule and sub-section, carries verifiable assertions, and identifies applicable PHI entity types.

regulation.name: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act

ai_specific_guidance.ocr_ai_bulletin_2024: In 2024, HHS OCR issued guidance clarifying that AI systems creating, receiving, maintaining, or transmitting PHI are subject to full HIPAA compliance — including LLM API calls that contain PHI. See: hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/special-topics/health-information-technology/index.html
ai_specific_guidance.llm_api_classification: Sending PHI to an LLM API (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) constitutes 'disclosure' under 45 CFR 164.502. The LLM vendor becomes a Business Associate and requires a BAA. Alternatively, PHI must be de-identified per §164.514 before transmission.

penalty_tiers.description: Did not know and could not have known
Reasonable cause but not wilful neglect
Wilful neglect but corrected within 30 days

hipaa_rules.privacy_rule: 45 CFR 164.500–164.534 — governs use and disclosure of PHI
hipaa_rules.enforcement_rule: 45 CFR 160.300–160.552 — governs HHS enforcement and penalties

controls.title: De-identify PHI before transmitting to LLM APIs
controls.description: PHI must be de-identified before being transmitted to LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, etc.) unless a BAA is in place. HIPAA §164.514 provides two safe harbors: (1) Expert Determination: a qualified statistician certifies re-identification risk is 'very small'; (2) Safe Harbor: removal of all 18 PHI identifiers. For AI systems, the Safe Harbor method — automated PII redaction — is the only practical approach at scale.
safe_harbor_18_identifiers: Geographic subdivisions smaller than a state
Dates (except year) related to the individual
Any other unique identifying number or code

controls.title: Business Associate Agreement with LLM API vendors
controls.condition: If PHI is transmitted to any LLM API or AI service provider
controls.description: Any vendor that creates, receives, maintains, or transmits PHI on behalf of a Covered Entity is a Business Associate and requires a signed BAA. This includes: LLM APIs (if PHI is in prompts), AI model providers, cloud storage for PHI, analytics platforms receiving PHI. The BAA must specify: permitted uses, safeguard requirements, PHI return/destruction, breach notification obligation.

implementation.note: LLM vendor BAA status: OpenAI (openai.com/security/hipaa), Google Cloud Healthcare API (available), Azure OpenAI (available via Azure BAA), Anthropic (check current status at anthropic.com). Best practice: use de-identification (HIPAA-AI-001) so BAA scope is minimised.
implementation.best_practice: Zero-PHI API calls via svitch.wrap() eliminates BAA dependency for LLM API tier

controls.title: Minimum necessary PHI in AI system inputs
controls.description: HIPAA requires that only the minimum necessary PHI be used or disclosed for the intended purpose. For AI systems, this means: (a) do not include full patient records in prompts when a summary suffices; (b) do not pass PHI to AI tools that don't require it for their function; (c) policy-based field selection: define which PHI fields each agent or tool is permitted to access.

controls.title: Access controls for AI systems handling ePHI
controls.description: Covered Entities must implement technical policies to allow access to ePHI only to authorized users. For AI systems, this means: unique agent identities, access logging, role-based data access (agent X may only access PHI categories Y), and automatic session termination. LLM API keys must not be shared across agents with different PHI access levels.

implementation.note: agent_id functions as unique agent identity in audit trail

controls.title: Audit log for AI system PHI access
controls.description: Covered Entities must implement hardware, software, and procedural mechanisms to record and examine activity in systems that contain or use ePHI. For AI systems, this requires an immutable audit log recording: which agent accessed which PHI, when, for what purpose, which LLM received the (de-identified) data, and the outcome of each decision. The log must be tamper-evident.

retention.note: HIPAA requires retention of policies and documentation for 6 years from creation or last effective date. State law may require longer retention for medical records.

implementation.sdk_method: run.verify() — returns valid=True if Merkle chain is intact

controls.title: Integrity of ePHI in AI pipelines
controls.description: Covered Entities must protect ePHI from improper alteration or destruction. For AI systems, this means: (a) AI-generated clinical recommendations must not overwrite authoritative PHI records without human review; (b) audit logs must be hash-chained so tampering is detectable; (c) AI outputs that update patient records must carry provenance metadata.

implementation.sdk_method: run.human_checkpoint(question, approved, reviewer_id) before any PHI update

controls.title: Encryption of ePHI in transit to LLM APIs
controls.description: ePHI transmitted over electronic networks must be protected against unauthorised access. All LLM API calls must use TLS 1.2+. Even when PHI is de-identified before transmission, the channel must be encrypted because de-identification is not perfect and residual risk may remain. Do not use HTTP endpoints for AI API calls.

implementation.note: Standard HTTPS. Verify via: openssl s_client -connect api.openai.com:443 -tls1_2

controls.title: Breach notification for PHI exposed by AI systems
controls.description: A breach of unsecured PHI must be notified to: (a) affected individuals within 60 days of discovery; (b) HHS Secretary — within 60 days if affecting 500+ individuals, or annually if affecting fewer; (c) prominent media if 500+ residents of a state. For AI systems, an inadvertent PHI disclosure to an LLM API (e.g., un-redacted prompt) likely constitutes a breach unless the low probability exception applies. The audit trail makes breach scope determination possible.
controls.low_probability_exception: A breach does not require notification if there is a low probability that the PHI has been compromised, assessed by: nature of PHI disclosed, who received it, whether PHI was actually acquired, extent of risk mitigated.

implementation.sdk_method: run.verify() — tamper-evident chain enables precise breach scope determination

controls.title: Risk analysis covering AI system PHI exposure
controls.description: Covered Entities must conduct a thorough and accurate risk analysis of potential risks and vulnerabilities to ePHI. This must now include AI-specific risks: (a) PHI leakage through LLM prompt injection; (b) PHI in LLM context windows or model weights if fine-tuning; (c) PHI in LLM vendor logs; (d) model inversion attacks on fine-tuned models; (e) re-identification risk from de-identified data in AI outputs.
ai_specific_risks: PHI in LLM vendor request logs (even if de-identified data is re-identifiable)
PHI leakage through LLM hallucination or training data memorisation
Re-identification from AI outputs combining quasi-identifiers
Unauthorised agent access to PHI data sources
AI model fine-tuned on PHI becoming a PHI store

controls.title: HIPAA training for AI/ML team members handling PHI
controls.description: All workforce members with access to PHI must receive HIPAA training. For AI/ML teams, this must cover AI-specific HIPAA obligations: no PHI in LLM prompts without BAA/de-identification, proper handling of model training data, incident reporting for accidental PHI exposure. Training must be documented.

implementation.note: Administrative control. Svitch audit trail logs who accessed PHI and when, supporting training compliance verification.

controls.title: Human oversight for AI-generated clinical decisions
controls.rule: Privacy Rule (minimum necessary) + FDA guidance on Clinical Decision Support
controls.description: While HIPAA does not explicitly mandate human oversight of AI clinical decisions, the FDA's guidance on Clinical Decision Support Software (2022) requires non-locked CDS software that could affect patient safety to be reviewed by a clinician. Combined with HIPAA minimum necessary and integrity requirements, AI-generated clinical recommendations used to update patient records should have documented human review.

controls.title: Contingency plan for AI system PHI availability
controls.description: Covered Entities must have contingency plans to ensure availability of ePHI in emergencies. For AI systems that are part of PHI workflows (e.g., AI-assisted clinical documentation), the plan must address: (a) fallback to non-AI workflows; (b) audit trail backup and recovery; (c) AI system failure mode that does not corrupt or lose PHI.

implementation.note: Administrative control. Svitch audit trail export to immutable storage (S3 Object Lock, GCS Retention Policy) satisfies audit trail backup requirement.

hipaa_18_safe_harbor.note: NER model recommended; regex alone insufficient for names

hipaa_18_safe_harbor.description: DOB or dates related to individual
hipaa_18_safe_harbor.note: Date patterns require context to distinguish PHI dates from other dates
